agents.name: claude
agents.description: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed.

agents.name: Explore
agents.description: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.description: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.

agents.name: Plan
agents.description: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

agents.name: statusline-setup
agents.description: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting.

Canada is the second-largest country in the world by total area, spanning approximately 9.98 million square kilometers across North America. Here's a detailed overview:

## Geography
Canada stretches from the Atlantic Ocean in the east to the Pacific Ocean in the west, and from the US border in the south to the Arctic Ocean in the north. It encompasses diverse landscapes including the Rocky Mountains, the Canadian Shield, vast prairies, and numerous coastlines. The country contains about 31% of the world's fresh water and is home to the Great Lakes (shared with the US).

## Population & Regions
With a population of approximately 40 million people, Canada has 10 provinces and 3 territories. Major cities include Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Calgary, and Ottawa (the capital). The country has significant geographic variation, from temperate coastal regions to subarctic and arctic climates.

## History
Originally inhabited by Indigenous peoples for thousands of years, Canada was colonized by French and British explorers starting in the 17th century. It gradually gained independence from Britain, with Confederation occurring in 1867. The country maintained ties to the British Commonwealth and adopted a constitutional monarchy.

## Government
Canada operates as a federal parliamentary democracy with a Westminster-style system. The Prime Minister is the head of government, while the monarch (currently King Charles III) is the ceremonial head of state, represented by a Governor General.

## Economy
Canada has one of the world's largest economies, driven by natural resources (oil, natural gas, minerals), agriculture, manufacturing, and services. It's a G7 member and has strong trade relationships, particularly with the United States through the USMCA (formerly NAFTA).

## Culture & Society
Canada is known for multiculturalism and bilingualism (English and French). It's relatively progressive on social issues and is recognized globally for quality of life. Indigenous cultures remain an important part of Canadian identity.

## Natural Resources & Climate
The country is resource-rich with vast forests, mineral deposits, and energy reserves. Climate varies dramatically by region, from temperate rainforests on the west coast to arctic tundra in the north, with most populated areas experiencing significant seasonal variation.
